title.narrative: ILO/KGRTC PPDP "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa” (SESA)
ILO/KGRTC PPDP "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa” (SESA)

description.narrative: Insatsen - "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa" (SESA) är ett drygt treårigt program för att i samverkan med näringslivet utforma och genomföra utbildningar inom förnybar energiteknik och energiefektivisering, med International Labout Organization ILO och SADC-institutionen Kafue Gorge Regional Training Centre KGRTC.

The contribution - "Skills for Energy in Southern Africa” (SESA) intervention is a Public-Private Development Partnership (PPDP) that enables a transfer of technical skills from international and local energy companies to power technicians and managers in Southern Africa through International Labour Organization (ILO) and in partnership with SADC’s Kafue Gorge Regional Training Centre (KGRTC) in Zambia.

"Skills for Energy in Southern Africa (SESA) is a Public-Private Development Partnership (PPDP) that enables a transfer of technical skills from international and local energy companies to power technicians and managers in Southern Africa through International Labour Organization (ILO) and in partnership with SADCs Kafue Gorge Regional Training Centre (KGRTC) in Zambia.
The focus is on contributing to SDG 7 on universal access to modern energy, by responding to the power industry's needs for skills development in the areas of renewable energy, energy efficiency and regional energy integration, but also to SDG 4 on skills and training, and SDG 8 on sustainable economic growth, productive employment and decent work. The expected impact is an increased uptake of renewable energy, energy efficiency and regional energy integration interventions in Southern Africa, leading to more sustainable use of energy and a low carbon energy mix.
The four-year project will facilitate partnerships between KGRTC and the private sector, strengthen KGRTCs capacity to enable it to be - and to be perceived as - the Centre of Excellence for energy training in the region and will result in around 1000 power technicians, engineers and managers that are skilled in, and able to apply, up-to-date technologies in renewable energy, energy efficiency and regional energy integration.
Overall Objective Increase uptake of Renewable Energy (RE), Energy Efficiency (EE) and Regional Energy Integration (REI) interventions in Southern Africa, leading to a more sustainable and low-carbon energy mix.
Specific objectives (Outcomes) Outcome 1: More power engineers, technicians and managers in the SADC region have enhanced technical capacity to apply, manage and promote the latest RE, EE and REI technologies. Outcome 2: KGRTC has built its brand and standing as the regions Centre of Excellence for competitive skills training in RE, EE and REI technologies.

sector.narrative: Energy generation, renewable sources - multiple technologies

description.narrative:
The intervention is on a satisfactory path towards its objective, and has delivered on both of its outcome goals. For most parts, it is considered as likely that the intervention will meets its objectives.
Outcome 1: The project has developed in total 26 high-quality courses in the three thematic focus areas of RE, EE and REI technologies, contributing to workforce development in the energy sector in the region. In 2023, training was provided to 123 engineers, technicians and energy managers, resulting in a cumulative total of 400 trained individuals, representing 39% of the target of 1014 participants. In terms of gender balance, the program has a notable inclusion of 159 female course participants. This corresponds to 40%, which surpasses the project's initial target of 25% female participation by 15%.
In 2023, the project conducted an extensive tracer study to evaluate the impact of KGRTC training programs under the SESA project. This study reached 121 participants and 61% out of these, i.e 75 persons, have initiated or supported projects in RE, EE and/or REI since they participated in the course. Furthermore, the project engaged with various power utilities and private companies, seeking their feedback on the relevance of the courses offered. 100% of respondents from these entities expressed satisfaction, affirming that the courses provided are highly relevant to their industry demands. This positive feedback from the sector stakeholders highlights the practical applicability and industry alignment of the training programs.
Outcome 2: A critical outcome of the SESA project is the enhancement of KGRTC's institutional capacity. In 2023, the development and launch of new KGRTC Website took place. It is designed to significantly boost KGRTC's visibility and enhances user experience and interaction, particularly with the integration of the E-campus feature marking a substantial stride in digital outreach. The project has also facilitated the transition to a digital follow-up system for KGRTC trainees. This upgrade addresses needs in data storage and enables more efficient reporting on trainee outcomes and behaviours, representing a significant improvement in the institution's operational efficiency.
In line with the PPDP approach, the project has successfully established a total of fifteen (15) active partnerships. This network of partnerships includes seven (7) Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) and eight (8) Letters of Commitment. During 2023, these collaborations have made notable contributions in the development and validation of training programs. The partnerships have provided technical expertise and resources, including equipment and training sites, valued at approximately USD 117,229 for 2023 and USD 407,667 cumulatively for the project duration.
A Participatory Gender Audit training was conducted in July 2023 and KGRTC conducted an in-house Gender Audit in 2023. The Gender Policy will be developed by April 2024.
